name: How does framing a standard window compare to framing a basement egress window?

mainEntity.name: How does framing a standard window compare to framing a basement egress window?

acceptedAnswer.text: Framing a standard above-grade window involves wood-stud construction, whereas basement egress window framing requires cutting through solid poured concrete or cinder block foundations. Basement openings demand heavy concrete sawing, structural steel lintels or specialized headers, and exterior excavation down to the footing to install an egress window well and drainage system. Standard wood-framed openings focus primarily on stud shoring, header installation, exterior sheathing, and weather barriers without the heavy excavation and masonry work necessary for below-grade installations.
acceptedAnswer.description: Basement egress framing requires concrete foundation cutting, excavation, and window well drainage, whereas standard framing involves cutting wood studs and standard headers.
